messages:
csm-alex: Heads-up — enterprise customer seeing truncated JSON when streaming in structured output mode. They say the stream cuts off during an auth refresh and the final object is missing closing braces. request_id=req_9b2f, model=redwood-v1-chat, region=us-west-2. They attached a curl snippet that reproduces it locally.

maya: Ack. Is this via our JS SDK or raw HTTP? Any proxy in front of the client?

csm-alex: They're using our JS SDK 1.4.2 inside an Electron wrapper. There's a corporate proxy + their mobile app's auth layer that refreshes tokens automatically.

maya: Got it. Could be token rotation mid-stream sending a FIN/RST or the client re-establishing connection. Can you paste the customer's curl repro and the truncated output?

csm-alex: Pasting minimal repro (customer sanitized):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-v1-chat \
  -d '{"mode":"structured","prompt":"{...}"}' \
  --no-buffer
```
Observed last bytes: `...\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"...\\\"}},` then connection closed. Missing `]}\"` and trailing `}`.

derek: Can you also paste the tcpdump / proxy logs around req_9b2f? Need to know if we saw a 401 handshake midstream or a TLS-level close.

csm-alex: Attached cropped proxy log: `PROXY-12345: client_conn 10.2.3.4:52344 -> edge1:443 FIN from client at 15:02:12.345` then `EDGE: stream closed req=req_9b2f status=200 bytes_sent=3129`. No 401 on our side.

derek: Interesting — edge shows 200 and bytes_sent is lower than expected. That suggests client closed first (maybe due to token refresh) rather than server aborting. Do we see any mid-stream auth-banner or token refresh call from the SDK?

csm-alex: Customer says their SDK refresh kicks in on 401 responses, but they also observed an internal refresh timer that prematurely swaps the token when it nears expiry.

maya: Can you try a repro with a long-lived token (15m+) to rule out midstream rotation? Also try raw REST (no SDK) to see if the Electron wrapper is the culprit.

csm-alex: Ran quick test: long-lived token + identical curl -> stream completes and final JSON valid. So token swap looks likely.

sre-bot: [trace] req_9b2f found in proxy logs: client FIN observed at 2025-11-03T15:02:12Z; no midstream 401 from edge; backend reported graceful close after EOF. Trace: https://internal-traces/redwood/req_9b2f

derek: Thanks. Two hypotheses: 1) client-side token refresh triggers reconnect and drops existing socket, cutting off the SSE frame mid-object; 2) proxy or OS-level TCP keepalive timeout kills connection while kernel rebinds with new creds. Both result in truncated SSE payloads that leave partially emitted JSON.

maya: For mitigation we should advise customer to: 1) avoid rotating tokens mid-request; 2) if rotation is unavoidable, implement token refresh with a short grace period and only for new connections; 3) enable client-side buffering so final SSE event is allowed to finish before reconnect.

eng-runtime-oncall: Tagging eng-runtime for visibility — if clients are frequently closing mid-event we should detect partial SSE events and emit an explicit final error event like `data: {"error":"incomplete_stream","cause":"client_disconnect"}` when backend notices EOF before completing a top-level structured object. That would make parsing failures clearer to integrators.

derek: Agree — we can also add a heuristic: when structured mode is enabled, attempt to flush a final short keepalive/window (a single `\n\n` or small `data: {"heartbeat":true}` SSE frame) if EOF is seen, then emit an `incomplete` marker. Need to confirm impact on streaming cost and semantics.

maya: Meanwhile for support action items:
- Ask customer to reproduce with long-lived token + raw curl and attach full tcpdump.
- Provide them recommended SDK config to delay refresh mid-request (example below).

csm-alex: Sent recommended SDK snippet to customer:
```js
// JS SDK: set token refresh to only run between streams
sdk.setAuth({
  tokenRefresh: async (oldToken) => {
    // do not refresh if a stream is active
    if (sdk._activeStreams > 0) return oldToken;
    return await fetchNewToken();
  }
});
```

maya: Nice. Also told them to check Electron's network layer — sometimes it reuses a stale TLS session and forces reconnects.

eng-runtime-oncall: Filed ENG-RUNTIME-512 to evaluate adding explicit incomplete-stream markers + a flag `stream_strict=true` that would cause us to check structural completeness before closing. Assigning to @derek.

derek: I'll pick up ENG-RUNTIME-512. Short term: document best-practices in KB and add a note to structured-output docs about token rotation.

csm-alex: Customer confirmed they can repro reliably in 10/10 runs when their token refresh window is set to 1s before expiry. They will try long-lived token test and attach pcap.

maya: Great — flagging as high-priority until we get the pcap. Thanks everyone. :eyes: :pray:
